content.key_idea: By caching final images instead of model-specific latents, MoDM can serve cache-hit requests with a small model at full quality and short latency, unlike prior latent-caching work which still needs the large model even on cache hits.
content.reading_order: Top to bottom through three stacked rows: Baseline, Prior Work (Nirvana), MoDM (This Work), each read left to right from Prompt to Image.

summary: This figure introduces MoDM by contrasting it with two alternatives in three stacked rows. The Baseline row shows the basic latency/quality trade-off: a large model gives high quality but long latency, a small model gives low quality but short latency. The Prior Work (Nirvana) row shows latent-feature caching, where cache hits still route through the large model, only shortening the number of denoising steps and giving limited latency benefit. The MoDM row shows the paper's approach: an image cache stores final generated images; cache misses go to the large model for full-quality inference, while cache hits go to a small model that refines the retrieved cached image in fewer denoising steps, achieving high quality at short latency. The diagram uses flat rounded boxes, blue/green model color-coding, and colored text callouts for quality and latency.
summary_zh: 该图通过三行对比引出MoDM：基线展示大模型高质量高延迟、小模型低质量低延迟的权衡；先前工作Nirvana的隐特征缓存在命中时仍需大模型，收益有限；MoDM缓存最终图像，缓存命中时用小模型精炼，兼顾高质量与短延迟。
